title: 1977 AHSME Problem 22
statement: If \(f(x)\) is a real-valued function of the real variable \(x,\) and \(f(x)\) is not identically zero, and for all \(a\) and \(b\) \[ \begin{gathered} f(a+b)+f(a-b)\\ =2f(a)+2f(b), \end{gathered} \] then for all \(x\) and \(y\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: there is a positive number \(T\) such that \(f(x+T)=f(x)\)

solutions.text:
Setting \(a=b=0\) gives \(2f(0)=4f(0),\) so \(f(0)=0.\) Now set \(a=0\) and \(b=x.\) The equation becomes \[ \begin{aligned} f(x)+f(-x) &=2f(0)+2f(x)\\ &=2f(x), \end{aligned} \] and hence \(f(-x)=f(x)\) for every real \(x.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
